questions.question: In this question, a statement is followed by two arguments numbered I and II. Based on the statement, you have to decide which of the arguments is strong. Statement: Should there be a ceiling on the salaries of top executives of multinationals in our country? Arguments: I. Yes. Otherwise, it would lead to unhealthy competition and our own industry would not be able to withstand that. II. No. With the accent on liberalization of the economy, any such move would be counter-productive. Once the economy picks up, this disparity will be reduced.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, a statement is followed by two arguments numbered I and II. Based on the statement, you have to decide which of the arguments is strong.

Statement: Should there be a ceiling on the salaries of top executives of multinationals in our country?

Arguments:

I. Yes. Otherwise, it would lead to unhealthy competition and our own industry would not be able to withstand that.

II. No. With the accent on liberalization of the economy, any such move would be counter-productive. Once the economy picks up, this disparity will be reduced.

options.text: If only argument I is strong.
options.html: If only argument I is strong.

options.text: If only conclusion II is strong.
options.html: If only conclusion II is strong.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: If both (I) and (II) are strong.

In the absence of such a ceiling, the companies would be involved in a mutual competition of salaries, in a bid to attract the most competent professionals. So, an argument I hold. Also, the prospects of increase in salary would encourage the officials to perform better in the interest of the company they serve, which would otherwise not be so if a ceiling is imposed. So, argument II also holds strong.

questions.question: Select the option that indicates the correct arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Flower 2. Bees 3. Seed 4. Nectar 5. Honey
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that indicates the correct arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order.
1. Flower
2. Bees
3. Seed
4. Nectar
5. Honey
questions.solution:
Here's the logical sequence:

Seed (3): The process begins with the seed, which can grow into a plant.

Flower (1): The seed grows into a flower, which is the reproductive part of the plant.

Nectar (4): Flowers produce nectar, which attracts pollinators.

Bees (2): Bees are attracted to the nectar and visit the flowers.

Honey (5): Bees collect nectar from flowers and convert it into honey.

So, the logical order is from seed to flower, then nectar attracts bees, which in turn produce honey.
